# `silk/mem/shared`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Shared ownership of one mutable value on one thread, with access through callbacks.

## When to use
Use [`Shared`](#Shared) when several values that you own separately, such as stored callbacks or
computations that run later, must all use the same mutable state, and a borrow cannot live long
enough. For one owner, use the value directly or `silk.mem.box.Box`.

## Details
[`Shared.make`](#Shared.impl.make) allocates one time. [`Shared.clone`](#Shared.impl.clone), [`Shared.with`](#Shared.impl.with), and [`Shared.withMut`](#Shared.impl.withMut) do
not allocate. Each handle counts as one owner. When you drop a handle that is not the last one,
the value stays. When you drop the last handle, the value is dropped and the allocation is
released. A handle stays on the thread that made it.

Access is exclusive for the duration of the callback, also for [`Shared.with`](#Shared.impl.with). A nested access
to the same value through any handle traps before the nested callback starts. This applies to
all four combinations of `with` and `withMut`.

## Gotchas
Handles that refer to each other in a cycle are never dropped, so the value leaks until you
break the cycle. There are no weak handles. Do not call code that can access the same value from
inside a callback. Get the data you need, return from the callback, and then call that code.

## Examples
### Update a value through one handle and read it through another
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.shared { Shared }

struct Counter {
  value: i32,
}

fn addTwo(counter: &mut Counter) -> i32 {
  counter.value = counter.value + 2
  return counter.value
}

fn read(counter: &Counter) -> i32 {
  return counter.value
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let first = run Shared<Counter>.make(Counter { value: 40 })
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let second = Shared<Counter>.clone(&first)
  let updated = Shared<Counter>.withMut<i32>(&second, addTwo)
  if updated != 42 || Shared<Counter>.with<i32>(&first, read) != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Shared` with `import silk.mem.shared { Shared }`.

## `Shared`

```silk
pub struct Shared<T>
```

A strong handle to one value of type `T` that other handles can also own.

### When to use

Use it when several values that you own separately, such as stored callbacks or computations
that run later, must all use the same mutable state, and a borrow cannot live long enough. For
one owner, use the value directly or `silk.mem.box.Box`.

### Details

Drop is automatic. The value is dropped when the last handle is dropped. A handle cannot move to
another thread.

[`Shared.make`](#Shared.impl.make) allocates one time. [`Shared.clone`](#Shared.impl.clone), [`Shared.with`](#Shared.impl.with), and [`Shared.withMut`](#Shared.impl.withMut) do
not allocate. Access is exclusive for the duration of the callback, also for [`Shared.with`](#Shared.impl.with). A
nested access to the same value through any handle traps before the nested callback starts.

### Gotchas

Handles that refer to each other in a cycle are never dropped, so the value leaks until you
break the cycle. There are no weak handles.

## Implementation `Shared<T>`

```silk
impl<T> Shared<T>
```

<a id="Shared.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn make<'env>(value: T) -> Shared<T> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Allocates storage, moves `value` into it, and returns the first handle.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the storage. No handle is made, and
  `value` is dropped.

#### Details

The handle does not keep a reference to the allocator after `make` returns.

<a id="Shared.impl.clone"></a>

### Method `clone`

```silk
pub fn clone(self: &Self) -> Shared<T>
```

Returns a new handle to the same value. It does not allocate and does not touch the value.

#### Gotchas

If the handle count reaches its maximum, `clone` traps before it changes the count.

<a id="Shared.impl.withMut"></a>

### Method `withMut`

```silk
pub fn withMut<A>(self: &Self, use: once fn(&mut T) -> A) -> A
```

Calls `use` one time with a mutable borrow of the value and returns the result of `use`.

#### Details

The borrow cannot escape the callback, and it cannot stay live across a suspension.

#### Gotchas

If `use` accesses the same value again through any handle, the program traps before the nested
callback starts.

<a id="Shared.impl.with"></a>

### Method `with`

```silk
pub fn with<A>(self: &Self, use: once fn(&T) -> A) -> A
```

Calls `use` one time with a shared borrow of the value and returns the result of `use`.

#### Details

`with` uses [`Shared.withMut`](#Shared.impl.withMut) internally, so the access is exclusive for the duration of the
callback. The callback cannot change the value through its `&T`.

#### Gotchas

A nested access to the same value through any handle traps, also when both accesses use
`with`.
